faqs.q: How long does a natural slate roof last on an older Orange home?

runs.v: Natural slate lasts 60 to 150 years, premium slate often 100-plus, per InterNACHI and the National Slate Association; the fasteners and flashing wear out first.

faqs.q: Can individual broken slates on my Orange roof be repaired without replacing the whole roof?

runs.v: Yes. A slate roof can be repaired tile by tile: a cracked slate comes out with a slate ripper and a matched slate goes in without disturbing its neighbors.

faqs.q: Does slate roofing work in an Orange historic district require special approval?

runs.v: It can. Confirm the property's local historic status with the City of Orange Township before exterior roofing, since historic-district work can need review.

faqs.q: Why does my Orange slate roof leak when most of the tiles look intact?

runs.v: The biggest problem with slate roofs is rarely the stone: corroded fasteners and degraded flashing fail first and cause the leaks.

faqs.q: Can my Orange house support the weight of a slate roof?

runs.v: Only after a structural check, since slate weighs far more than asphalt shingles. On buildings other than detached one- and two-family homes, the 25% rule of N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 requires a permit to repair more than 25% of the roof area in 12 months; as a rule of thumb, damage over 25% also favors replacement, though slate often stays repairable.

faqs.q: How much does slate roof installation repair cost in Orange, NJ?
